newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL says pipeline system back to normal.
newsitem.headline: IPL says pipeline system back to normal.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said Thursday its huge crude oil and products pipeline system returned to normal operations after its major shutdown this week..

"We do have some very minor issues to be resolved at Clearbrook (Minnesota), but for throughputs and rates on the various lines we are back to normal operations on our pipeline system," IPL said on its shipper hotline.
IPL's total throughput from its numerous pipeline segements that extend to southern Ontatrio and the U.S. Midwest from western Canada is about 1.4 million barrels per day.

Volumes on the system, the world's longest for crude oil and petroleum products, were brought to a standstill when a power outage in storm-battered Minnesota last weekend knocked out four pumping stations.
The company had been scrambling since Sunday to fix the situation, which was made worse by the difficulty utilities had restoring power to their market areas in the wake of the freak spring storm.
The IPL shutdown initially forced to a halt one million barrels of oil, which is equal to about half of Canada's total daily production.
